question.text: Under FATF Special Recommendation VI (SR VI), persons or legal entities that provide money or value transmission services, including any informal money or value transfer system or network, are required to be:

answer.text: Licensed or registered by a competent authority
Self-certified with a declaration filed to the central bank
Exempt from regulation if operating below a specified threshold
Only registered but not required to be licensed

explanation.text: The Logic: SR VI requires that persons or legal entities providing money or value transmission services, including any informal money or value transfer system or network, should be licensed or registered and subject to all applicable FATF Recommendations. The Trap: "Self-certified" is too weak a standard. "Exempt from regulation" is the opposite of SR VI's intent. "Only registered" is incomplete - the source allows either licensing OR registration. Note: SR VI gives countries flexibility on the licensing-versus-registration mechanism, provided the relevant FATF Recommendations apply to those services.
